title: Metamorphic Safety Relations: Testing LLM Consistency Without Ground Truth

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Downgraded. LLMORPH already implements metamorphic testing for LLMs with 36 relations and 561K test groups. The safety-specific application is a minor extension.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building relation-preserving transforms (paraphrase, translation, code vs. prose) uses available NLP tools. Running pairs through a model and checking consistency is basic scripting. LLMORPH provides a template. Accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: violation rate for a set of metamorphic safety relations on a specific model. Single experiment with well-defined metric. Library of transforms can be kept small for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: LLMORPH (ASE 2025, ICSME 2025) implements exactly this: 36 metamorphic relations, 561,297 test groups across three LLMs and four NLP tasks, finding 18% average failure rate and 11% failures missed by traditional testing. 'Metamorphic Testing of Large Language Models for Natural Language Processing' (ICSME 2025) provides the first systematic literature search on MRs for NLP, cataloging 191 unique MRs. 'Bias Testing and Mitigation in Black Box LLMs using Metamorphic Relations' (arXiv:2512.00556, 2025) applies metamorphic testing specifically for fairness evaluation. 'Effectiveness of symmetric metamorphic relations on validating the stability of code generation LLM' (2024) addresses code generation stability. The proposed idea — applying metamorphic relations to test safety consistency — is a specific application of an already-published and well-characterized framework.
